steps.note: K.1.1.1 states the net target change (JV+RG)x independent of the initial scratch vectors a,c, and its quote gives the subtract/add/restore rows.
K.1.1.2 gives the bit central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, the side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, and self coefficient one.
K.1.1.2 gives the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, with its quote stating the side cancels intersections zero and two.
K.1.1.3 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

The plan says every edge joins comparable labels and that the other residuals 'follow by splitting A=B perp P and F=<t> perp t^perp' (K.1.4.1, K.1.4.2), but it never gives the per-edge residuals and their dimensions.
K.1.4.2 states t_X perp t_Y gives <t_X> subset t_Y^perp, and its quote gives the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2.
The plan states that center 3->4 is the only decreasing edge, losing h, and that telescoping gives sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N and absolute Wm-2N+2L.
K.1.4.1 only asserts that every nonzero binary residual has an orthonormal basis; the nondegenerate/nonalternating argument and the absorption of alternating planes are missing.
S0.3.1.1 derives weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors and q_V-q_U = sum_v wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal residual basis.
S0.3.1.2 states wt(v) odd, the phase i^{eps[v.x]} as a combination of 1 and (-1)^{v.x}, and H diag(1,-1) H = X giving aI+bX_v or its inverse.

S0.3.2.4 makes the frame the tensor product over the f columns, with one child (C^{eps})^{tensor f} acting on all columns per residual basis vector; S0.3.2.7 gives s_c such factors in all. This is the paper's k-column statement, used where the recursion uses it.

S0.3.1.3 gives frame I for the zero label and C^{tensor m} for the full label, and C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a). Its quote has Z_{a,k} before, i^{27k} Z_{a,k} after and C=iZC^{-1}Z, and it negates the X outputs.
The plan states that both loss ratios are below 1/2, that the deficit is N-2L_b>0 and that s_b < W_b m.
K.2 names the 'exact relative deficit eta_b' but never gives its value 339/22587335000000.
The value eta_c=73/19906842167500 appears nowhere; eta_c occurs only in K.2's quote, as 'either eta=eta_b or eta=eta_c'.
K.2 and its quote state that both deficits exceed 20*2^-50 and that log m<20, so m^{1-2^-50} > m(1-eta) and s/W < m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.
K.3.1.1 and K.3.1.2 give the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing by lower-triangular elementary operations, repetition on the active indices, and exactly a ones in Pi.
K.3.2 states a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators and the diagonal numerators of a finite table, so the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.
K.3.3 states that a lower-triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order.
K.3.4 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j: one interchange per one of Pi, a in all.
The plan gives E=64(W+m+1)^3 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}), and elsewhere C_1=20. It never defines C_0=128mB^2, nu=min{j: m^j>=B} or C_1=max{20,nu+3}; B=s+E appears only inside a quoted inequality.
S0.3.5.1 bounds the per-invocation count 24W^3+4s+4W+4 below E, and S0.3.5.2 states A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e)<=8e at a leaf.
S0.3.5.2 gives B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu and A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and S0.3.5.3 keeps the total below 128mB^2 d^{nu+3} <= C_0 d^{C_1}.
S0.3.5.4 gives depth ell values in 2^{-(p+ell)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^ell and the exact p+Delta / Delta+3 bit reservation; S0.3.5.5 uses eps C_1<1 to get Delta=o(p).
S0.3.6.4 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and truncation errs by less than sqrt2 2^-p.

summary: P09 is detailed and quote-backed. It has 21 of 26 sub-steps present, none wrong. Absent: L1 (no per-edge residual table), L4 (orthonormal basis asserted without the nonalternating argument), R2 and R3 (the exact eta values never given) and S1 (C_0, nu and C_1=max{20,nu+3} never defined).
